rows.name: Steakhouse Financial
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on Base rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $0.50 to $3 if you bridge onto Base. Time: 10 minutes.

Open the curator's own vault list and pick the vault on Base with the deepest TVL and the shortest redemption delay; note its fee and its underlying lending market before you deposit anything. Cost: nothing to read the vault page. Time: 20 minutes.

Deposit $200 of USDC into that vault and keep the vault shares in the same wallet: the deposit is the position a curator's own launch would count. Cost: $200 of capital plus $0.02 to $0.20 of gas for the approval and the deposit. Time: 15 minutes.

Spread a second, smaller position across the curator's vaults on Ethereum, Robinhood Chain and Arbitrum so the activity is not one chain's snapshot; keep the two positions in the same wallet. Cost: another $100 of capital plus $0.50 to $3 to move it and $0.02 to $0.20 to deposit. Time: 30 minutes.

If the curator publishes a curator or delegate application, apply with the same wallet and the same address history: the application is free, and it is the only route from depositor to the role a launch would reward. Cost: nothing but the form, and no deposit is required to apply. Time: 30 minutes, then however long their review takes.

Re-check the vault every week: a curator's book can be withdrawn from a lending market under it, and a vault whose TVL falls by a third is a vault to leave before the redemption queue fills. Cost: under $0.80 of gas for a weekly check and any rebalance. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $2.75B of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 45 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $200 stays committed until you close. Time: 45 days, then 15 minutes to close.

rows.name: USDD
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on Tron rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $2 to $8 if you bridge onto Tron. Time: 10 minutes.

Open a position against the collateral the protocol accepts on Tron: deposit $300 of it, mint no more than a third of its value in the protocol's stable asset, and keep the rest of the collateral unused. Cost: $300 of collateral plus $0.30 to $2 of gas for the deposit and the mint. Time: 20 minutes.

Put the minted stable asset to work rather than leaving it idle: supply it back into a lending market on the same chain, and keep the two positions in one wallet so the health factor is one number to watch. Cost: $0.30 to $2 of gas to supply the minted asset, and no extra capital. Time: 15 minutes.

Check the health factor every week and keep it above 1.5; a market whose collateral price falls 30% in a week liquidates a position that was safe when it opened. Cost: $1 to $6 of gas for the weekly check and any top-up. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw in two steps rather than one: repay the borrow first, then the supply, so no hour passes with collateral posted against a debt you have already closed. Cost: $0.30 to $2 of gas for the repay and $0.30 to $2 for the withdrawal. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $1.06B of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

rows.name: BitFi Basis
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on BNB Chain rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $1 to $4 if you bridge onto Binance. Time: 10 minutes.

Open the two legs together on Binance: buy $100 of the spot asset and short the same dollar amount of its perpetual on the venue, so the position is flat on price and earns the funding instead. Cost: $100 of capital plus $0.05 to $0.30 of gas for the spot leg and the venue's own trading fee. Time: 30 minutes.

Keep margin on the short leg above the venue's maintenance requirement by a wide margin: a basis trade is safe on price and still liquidated when the short leg runs out of margin in a squeeze. Cost: about a third of the position held as margin, and $0.05 to $0.30 to top it up. Time: 15 minutes to set the buffer.

Check the funding rate every week and close the trade when it turns negative: a basis position pays while funding is positive and costs you while it is not, so the exit is a signal, not a date. Cost: $0.20 to $1 of gas and the venue's fees on each rebalance. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Unwind both legs in one session, spot first and short second, so the position is never naked on one side for longer than a single block. Cost: $0.05 to $0.30 of gas and the venue's closing fee. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $215M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Supply $150 of USDC to the market on Ethereum and note the utilisation of the pool you entered: above 90% utilisation the withdrawal is a queue, not a click. Cost: $150 of capital plus $2 to $12 of gas for the approval and the supply. Time: 15 minutes.

Borrow a small amount against the supply, no more than a third of it, and supply that back: the borrow is the second action a lending market's own record counts, and it costs interest rather than capital. Cost: interest on the borrow, currently a few percent a year, plus $2 to $12 of gas. Time: 20 minutes.

Check the health factor every week and keep it above 1.5; a market whose collateral price falls 30% in a week liquidates a position that was safe when it opened. Cost: $8 to $40 of gas for the weekly check and any top-up. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw in two steps rather than one: repay the borrow first, then the supply, so no hour passes with collateral posted against a debt you have already closed. Cost: $2 to $12 of gas for the repay and $2 to $12 for the withdrawal. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $254M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 30 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $150 stays committed until you close. Time: 30 days, then 15 minutes to close.

rows.name: R25
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on its chain rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $1 to $6 if you bridge onto Pharos. Time: 10 minutes.

Read the protocol's own terms on Pharos first: which entity issues the asset, what the redemption window is, and whether the position needs a permissioned wallet. An RWA that cannot be redeemed in your jurisdiction is not a farm position. Cost: nothing to read the terms, and no deposit to check eligibility. Time: 30 minutes.

Mint or buy $100 of the protocol's yield asset and hold it in a wallet you control rather than in the protocol's own custody page, so the position survives the protocol's front end going down. Cost: $100 of capital plus $0.10 to $1 of gas for the mint or the swap. Time: 20 minutes.

Hold through at least one distribution or interest payment: the record that matters for an RWA is a holder across a payment date, and a position opened and closed between two of them leaves nothing behind. Cost: the $100 stays invested, and the issuer's fee comes out of the yield. Time: 60 days.

Start the redemption before you need the money: an RWA's exit runs through the issuer's own process and can take days to weeks, and it is the step that surprises people who treat it like a token swap. Cost: $0.10 to $1 of gas to redeem, plus whatever the issuer charges for an early exit. Time: 15 minutes to start, then the issuer's window.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $198M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 60 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $100 stays committed until you close. Time: 60 days, then 15 minutes to close.

rows.name: Tori Finance
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on Ethereum mainnet rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $5 to $20 if you bridge onto Ethereum. Time: 10 minutes.

Open the two legs together on Ethereum: buy $100 of the spot asset and short the same dollar amount of its perpetual on the venue, so the position is flat on price and earns the funding instead. Cost: $100 of capital plus $2 to $12 of gas for the spot leg and the venue's own trading fee. Time: 30 minutes.

Keep margin on the short leg above the venue's maintenance requirement by a wide margin: a basis trade is safe on price and still liquidated when the short leg runs out of margin in a squeeze. Cost: about a third of the position held as margin, and $2 to $12 to top it up. Time: 15 minutes to set the buffer.

Check the funding rate every week and close the trade when it turns negative: a basis position pays while funding is positive and costs you while it is not, so the exit is a signal, not a date. Cost: $8 to $40 of gas and the venue's fees on each rebalance. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Unwind both legs in one session, spot first and short second, so the position is never naked on one side for longer than a single block. Cost: $2 to $12 of gas and the venue's closing fee. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $77M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 90 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $100 stays committed until you close. Time: 90 days, then 15 minutes to close.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $280M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Find the pool on Ripple that holds most of this protocol's $28M of TVL, and read its fee tier and its current range before you add anything; a pool off its range earns fees on nothing. Cost: nothing to read the pool. Time: 20 minutes.

Add $50 of liquidity as a pair rather than a single asset, in the range you expect the price to hold for the next month, and approve only the two tokens the pool takes. Cost: $50 of capital plus $0.10 to $1 of gas for two approvals and the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Set a reminder to check the range twice a week: a position that drifts out of range stops earning and starts holding the losing side of the pair, which is the cost nobody quotes. Cost: $0.50 to $4 of gas for the rebalances, and the impermanent loss if the pair moves. Time: 10 minutes twice a week.

Claim the pool's fees and any emissions on the schedule the protocol publishes, not daily: a claim costs gas every time and the reward does not compound faster than the fee you pay to take it. Cost: $0.10 to $1 per claim, so claim monthly rather than weekly. Time: 15 minutes a month.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $28M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 30 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 30 days, then 15 minutes to close.

Supply $50 of USDC to the market on Solana and note the utilisation of the pool you entered: above 90% utilisation the withdrawal is a queue, not a click. Cost: $50 of capital plus under $0.02 of gas for the approval and the supply. Time: 15 minutes.

Borrow a small amount against the supply, no more than a third of it, and supply that back: the borrow is the second action a lending market's own record counts, and it costs interest rather than capital. Cost: interest on the borrow, currently a few percent a year, plus under $0.02 of gas. Time: 20 minutes.

Check the health factor every week and keep it above 1.5; a market whose collateral price falls 30% in a week liquidates a position that was safe when it opened. Cost: under $0.10 of gas for the weekly check and any top-up. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw in two steps rather than one: repay the borrow first, then the supply, so no hour passes with collateral posted against a debt you have already closed. Cost: under $0.02 of gas for the repay and under $0.02 for the withdrawal. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $49M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 60 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 60 days, then 15 minutes to close.

rows.name: Apex Omni
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on Arbitrum One rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $1 to $5 if you bridge onto Arbitrum. Time: 10 minutes.

Deposit $50 of USDC as margin on Arbitrum and read the venue's fee schedule and liquidation rules before the first trade; a perps venue's record counts volume, and volume is cheap only if the fees are. Cost: $50 of margin plus $0.05 to $0.40 of gas for the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Trade small and often rather than large and once: a position at 2x leverage survives a 40% wick, one at 10x does not, and the record counts the trade either way. Cost: the venue's taker fee on each trade, and no more than 2x leverage. Time: 15 minutes a week.

Keep a liquidation price you can watch: write the price at which the position dies next to the position, and close it yourself before the venue does. Cost: $0.05 to $0.40 of gas to close, and the funding you pay while it is open. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw the margin in one go at the end rather than leaving it: a perps venue is a trading venue, not a savings account, and idle margin earns nothing. Cost: $0.05 to $0.40 of gas for the withdrawal. Time: 15 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $27M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Find the pool on Hyperliquid L1 that holds most of this protocol's $13M of TVL, and read its fee tier and its current range before you add anything; a pool off its range earns fees on nothing. Cost: nothing to read the pool. Time: 20 minutes.

Add $50 of liquidity as a pair rather than a single asset, in the range you expect the price to hold for the next month, and approve only the two tokens the pool takes. Cost: $50 of capital plus under $0.05 of gas for two approvals and the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Set a reminder to check the range twice a week: a position that drifts out of range stops earning and starts holding the losing side of the pair, which is the cost nobody quotes. Cost: under $0.20 of gas for the rebalances, and the impermanent loss if the pair moves. Time: 10 minutes twice a week.

Claim the pool's fees and any emissions on the schedule the protocol publishes, not daily: a claim costs gas every time and the reward does not compound faster than the fee you pay to take it. Cost: under $0.05 per claim, so claim monthly rather than weekly. Time: 15 minutes a month.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $13M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 45 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 45 days, then 15 minutes to close.

Withdraw in two steps rather than one: repay the borrow first, then the supply, so no hour passes with collateral posted against a debt you have already closed. Cost: $0.10 to $1 of gas for the repay and $0.10 to $1 for the withdrawal. Time: 20 minutes.

Deposit $50 of USDC as margin on Arbitrum and read the venue's fee schedule and liquidation rules before the first trade; a perps venue's record counts volume, and volume is cheap only if the fees are. Cost: $50 of margin plus $0.05 to $0.40 of gas for the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Trade small and often rather than large and once: a position at 2x leverage survives a 40% wick, one at 10x does not, and the record counts the trade either way. Cost: the venue's taker fee on each trade, and no more than 2x leverage. Time: 15 minutes a week.

Keep a liquidation price you can watch: write the price at which the position dies next to the position, and close it yourself before the venue does. Cost: $0.05 to $0.40 of gas to close, and the funding you pay while it is open. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw the margin in one go at the end rather than leaving it: a perps venue is a trading venue, not a savings account, and idle margin earns nothing. Cost: $0.05 to $0.40 of gas for the withdrawal. Time: 15 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $7M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 45 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 45 days, then 15 minutes to close.

rows.name: BTCFi CDP
farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on its chain rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $1 to $6 if you bridge onto Bifrost Network. Time: 10 minutes.

Open a position against the collateral the protocol accepts on Bifrost Network: deposit $75 of it, mint no more than a third of its value in the protocol's stable asset, and keep the rest of the collateral unused. Cost: $75 of collateral plus $0.10 to $1 of gas for the deposit and the mint. Time: 20 minutes.

Put the minted stable asset to work rather than leaving it idle: supply it back into a lending market on the same chain, and keep the two positions in one wallet so the health factor is one number to watch. Cost: $0.10 to $1 of gas to supply the minted asset, and no extra capital. Time: 15 minutes.

Check the health factor every week and keep it above 1.5; a market whose collateral price falls 30% in a week liquidates a position that was safe when it opened. Cost: $0.50 to $4 of gas for the weekly check and any top-up. Time: 10 minutes a week.

Withdraw in two steps rather than one: repay the borrow first, then the supply, so no hour passes with collateral posted against a debt you have already closed. Cost: $0.10 to $1 of gas for the repay and $0.10 to $1 for the withdrawal. Time: 20 minutes.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $6M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 30 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 30 days, then 15 minutes to close.

Find the pool on Polygon that holds most of this protocol's $6M of TVL, and read its fee tier and its current range before you add anything; a pool off its range earns fees on nothing. Cost: nothing to read the pool. Time: 20 minutes.

Add $50 of liquidity as a pair rather than a single asset, in the range you expect the price to hold for the next month, and approve only the two tokens the pool takes. Cost: $50 of capital plus $0.01 to $0.10 of gas for two approvals and the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Set a reminder to check the range twice a week: a position that drifts out of range stops earning and starts holding the losing side of the pair, which is the cost nobody quotes. Cost: under $0.40 of gas for the rebalances, and the impermanent loss if the pair moves. Time: 10 minutes twice a week.

Claim the pool's fees and any emissions on the schedule the protocol publishes, not daily: a claim costs gas every time and the reward does not compound faster than the fee you pay to take it. Cost: $0.01 to $0.10 per claim, so claim monthly rather than weekly. Time: 15 minutes a month.

farm_steps: Use a wallet that holds only this farm's money and keep its seed phrase off this machine; fund it on Plume rather than bridging after you start. Cost: nothing to open the wallet, and about $1 to $4 if you bridge onto Plume Mainnet. Time: 10 minutes.

Find the pool on Plume Mainnet that holds most of this protocol's $5M of TVL, and read its fee tier and its current range before you add anything; a pool off its range earns fees on nothing. Cost: nothing to read the pool. Time: 20 minutes.

Add $50 of liquidity as a pair rather than a single asset, in the range you expect the price to hold for the next month, and approve only the two tokens the pool takes. Cost: $50 of capital plus $0.02 to $0.20 of gas for two approvals and the deposit. Time: 20 minutes.

Set a reminder to check the range twice a week: a position that drifts out of range stops earning and starts holding the losing side of the pair, which is the cost nobody quotes. Cost: under $0.80 of gas for the rebalances, and the impermanent loss if the pair moves. Time: 10 minutes twice a week.

Claim the pool's fees and any emissions on the schedule the protocol publishes, not daily: a claim costs gas every time and the reward does not compound faster than the fee you pay to take it. Cost: $0.02 to $0.20 per claim, so claim monthly rather than weekly. Time: 15 minutes a month.

Keep the position under about 1% of the protocol's $5M of TVL: above that your own entry and exit move the pool, and the slippage costs more than the position is likely to earn. Cost: no fee to size it, and slippage of a few tenths of a percent at this size. Time: 5 minutes.

Write the wallet, the dates, every transaction hash and the amount in a farm log, and set a reminder for day 45 so you unwind on purpose instead of forgetting the position. Cost: no fee for the log itself, though the $50 stays committed until you close. Time: 45 days, then 15 minutes to close.
